extra.message: The /ops/pulse endpoint catches all exceptions and returns str(exc) and exc.__class__.__name__ in a 500 JSON response, leaking internal debug information to the client.

cwe: CWE-209: Information Exposure Through an Error Message

extra.message: The /ops/wire endpoint logs the raw Authorization header and request body, exposing bearer tokens or credentials in application logs.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: The /ops/after endpoint returns a RedirectResponse built directly from the user-supplied lane query parameter, allowing open redirection to arbitrary URLs.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: The /ops/bundle endpoint reads arbitrary request body or blob query parameter, optionally base64-decodes it, and passes it to pickle.loads(), enabling remote code execution via unsafe deserialization.
The /ops/vault endpoint uses the user-controlled ref value to construct a filesystem path (BASE_EXPORT_DIR / f'{ref}.json') without sanitization, allowing path traversal to arbitrary locations.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: The /ops/vault endpoint writes user-supplied SSN and card numbers to a plaintext JSON file without encryption or access controls, exposing sensitive PII.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: The /ops/blurb endpoint renders a user-supplied card value through a Jinja2 template using the |safe filter, disabling auto-escaping and allowing reflected cross-site scripting.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: The /ops/jinja endpoint concatenates a user-supplied fragment directly into a Jinja2 template string and renders it, allowing server-side template injection and arbitrary code execution.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

extra.message: The /ops/dock endpoint writes the request body to BASE_EXPORT_DIR / name where name is a user-controlled query parameter, allowing path traversal and arbitrary file write.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: The /ops/shell endpoint constructs a shell command by concatenating the user-controlled host parameter ('ping -c 1 ' + host) and passes it to os.system(), allowing command injection.

cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

extra.message: The /ops/mongo endpoint takes a JSON payload and passes the user-controlled filter object directly to MongoDB find_one(), allowing NoSQL injection and unauthorized data access.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic

extra.message: The /ops/origin endpoint reflects the user-supplied Origin header into Access-Control-Allow-Origin and sets Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true, allowing any origin to make authenticated cross-origin requests.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: The /ops/trust endpoint uses ssl._create_unverified_context() and disables certificate verification when calling urllib.request.urlopen(), making the connection vulnerable to MITM attacks.
The /ops/xml endpoint parses user-supplied XML with an lxml parser configured with load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, and no_network=False, enabling XML external entity (XXE) attacks.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: The /ops/workset endpoint updates a dictionary containing authorization fields (role, tier, approved, balance) with arbitrary keys from the user-supplied JSON payload, allowing mass assignment and authorization bypass.
The /ops/badge endpoint compares the ops_badge cookie or x-ops-badge header against the hardcoded literal 'lead' to grant elevated access, allowing anyone who knows the value to bypass role checks.
The session cookie is set with secure=False, allowing the session token to be transmitted over unencrypted HTTP connections and exposed to network eavesdropping.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute

extra.message: The password reset flow writes the raw, unhashed reset token together with the user's email to a local log file, exposing account takeover tokens to anyone with filesystem access.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: Settings defines a default secret_key value ('dev-secret-please-change-in-production-this-is-not-safe'). If not overridden by environment, this hardcoded secret is used to sign session tokens and API key hashes, enabling forgery.
